regulations.area: Humboldt Bay to Cape Mendocino · California · Northern Groundfish Management Area
regulations.scope: Reviewed 2026 official recreational boat rules within the Crescent City–Del Norte and Humboldt Bay–Cape Mendocino browse footprints. In-season closures, exact MPA geometry, method, harbor and route clearance remain separate checks.
common_notes: Northern Management Area is Oregon border to 40°10′ N. MPA and federal closures are position- and method-specific. A boat depth limit is not a legal depth boundary.
A regional rules card is not an open-season or exact-position clearance. Fresh source status, MPA geometry, method and in-season access remain separate checks.

rules-gear.name: CDFW finfish gear and general rules
rules-gear.review_note: Reviewed 2026 CDFW general finfish gear: rockfish and lingcod aboard impose one-line/two-hook limits; salmon has separate Northern boat gear restrictions. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-invertebrates.name: CDFW invertebrate gear rules
rules-invertebrates.review_note: Reviewed current CDFW section 29.80 recreational trap, hoop, snare, marking and tending rules; a scheduled crab season does not authorize traps without current declarations. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-whales.name: CDFW whale-safe crab restrictions
rules-whales.review_note: Reviewed whale-safe fishery status and declaration process; Northern November 2026 recreational crab trap clearance cannot be presumed in September. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-health.name: CDFW fishery health closures
rules-health.review_note: Reviewed CDFW health notice index; shellfish and Dungeness health closures must be checked again on the actual trip date. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-ocean.name: CDFW official regulation index
rules-ocean.review_note: Reviewed CDFW ocean regulation index as a source directory; it does not grant position-specific fishing permission. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-groundfish.name: CDFW groundfish
rules-groundfish.review_note: Reviewed CDFW 2026 groundfish summary and linked Northern table; Northern boat season Apr–Dec all depths and species limits differ from Mendocino. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-inseason.name: CDFW in-season changes
rules-inseason.review_note: Reviewed dated CDFW in-season changes through September 2026, including Klamath salmon closure; later notices must be rechecked. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-salmon.name: CDFW salmon
rules-salmon.review_note: Reviewed CDFW 2026 salmon page: Klamath Management Zone has no remaining 2026 opener; Smith River mouth closure and one-rod/barbless Northern boat rules apply. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-crab.name: CDFW crab
rules-crab.review_note: Reviewed CDFW permanent redirect to the canonical crab page and its September 24 recreational regulations and FAQ. The normalized content hash matches the previously reviewed source; current season, gear, whale and health checks remain separate. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-book.name: CDFW 2026 ocean sport fishing booklet
rules-book.review_note: Reviewed original 2026 CDFW ocean booklet for California halibut, albacore, Dungeness and on-board gear/fillet requirements; regional notices remain controlling. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-proposals.name: California FGC rulemaking: effective and pending changes
rules-proposals.review_note: Reviewed 2026 Fish and Game Commission proposal index; proposed changes without an effective date were not treated as operative Northern rules. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-tuna-federal.name: Federal recreational Pacific tuna rules · 50 CFR 660.721
rules-tuna-federal.review_note: Reviewed current eCFR 50 CFR 660.721: 25 albacore north of Point Conception, with trip/day possession constraints and southern-EEZ exception. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-salmon-pdf.name: CDFW 2026 ocean salmon season flyer · August update
rules-salmon-pdf.review_note: Reviewed original August 19 2026 CDFW salmon flyer: Klamath summer guideline reached, no fall opening north of 38°02 N, and Smith/Klamath mouth closures. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-groundfish-pdf.name: CDFW Northern groundfish season table
rules-groundfish-pdf.review_note: Reviewed original January 1 2026 Northern table: Apr 1–Dec 31 at all depths, RCG ten with one copper/two canary/four vermilion-sunset, lingcod two at 22 inches, descending device. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-northern.name: CDFW Northern Region rules
rules-northern.review_note: Reviewed Northern regional page updated August 31: 42°–40°10 N, Klamath salmon closed, Dungeness closed with scheduled Nov 7 opening, Pacific halibut open subject to quota. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

mpa-pyramid.name: CDFW Pyramid Point SMCA
mpa-pyramid.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Pyramid Point SMCA page: only surf smelt dip/throw-net recreational exception; app excludes all MPA geometry from fishing targets. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

mpa-st-george.name: CDFW Point St. George Reef Offshore SMCA
mpa-st-george.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Point St George Reef Offshore SMCA page: salmon troll and Dungeness trap exceptions, plus tribal exemptions; app excludes all MPA geometry. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

mpa-reading.name: CDFW Reading Rock MPAs
mpa-reading.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Reading Rock SMR/SMCA page: SMR no take; SMCA has salmon, surf smelt and Dungeness exceptions; app excludes all MPA geometry. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

rules-pacific-halibut.name: CDFW Pacific halibut season and quota
rules-pacific-halibut.review_note: Reviewed CDFW Pacific halibut page: north of Point Arena Apr 1–Nov 15 or earlier quota closure, one fish no minimum length, one line with two hooks when angling. Rechecked unchanged hash in new Humboldt footprint review.

mpa-samoa.name: CDFW Samoa SMCA
mpa-samoa.review_note: Read current CDFW Samoa SMCA regulations: salmon trolling, surf smelt nets and Dungeness trap/hoop/hand are narrow recreational exceptions; rockfish and lingcod take is prohibited there. App policy excludes the whole mapped MPA.

mpa-south-humboldt.name: CDFW South Humboldt Bay SMRMA
mpa-south-humboldt.review_note: Read current CDFW South Humboldt Bay SMRMA regulations: marine take prohibited except waterfowl under general hunting rules and named tribal exemption; app excludes the mapped management area from target fishing.

mpa-south-cape.name: CDFW South Cape Mendocino SMR and special closures
mpa-south-cape.review_note: Read current CDFW South Cape Mendocino SMR page: reserve prohibits marine take; Sugarloaf Island has year-round 300 ft vessel restriction, Steamboat Rock Mar 1 to Aug 31 300 ft restriction; app excludes protected geometry.

lingcod.name: Lingcod
lingcod.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Northern Management Area.
lingcod.bag: 2 per person daily; 2 in possession. Separate from the 10-fish RCG limit.
details: Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting lingcod, or when lingcod are aboard. Your double-drop rig fits that limit.
Carry a descending device ready for immediate use.
Fillets aboard: at least 14 in, with all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

rockfish.name: Rockfish / rock cod
rockfish.season: Apr 1–Dec 31, 2026 · boat fishing at all depths in the Northern Management Area.
rockfish.bag: 10 total rockfish, cabezon and greenlings combined per person daily and in possession.
rockfish.size: No minimum length for retained rockfish. Species must be identified.
details: Within the 10: at most 1 copper, 2 canary, and 4 vermilion/sunset rockfish combined.
No retention of yelloweye, quillback, cowcod or bronzespotted rockfish.
Use one line with no more than two hooks when targeting rockfish, or when rockfish are aboard. Carry a descending device ready for use.
Retained rockfish fillets must have all skin attached.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

halibut.name: California halibut
halibut.season: California halibut: year-round in the reviewed 2026 Northern rules; distinct from Pacific halibut.
halibut.bag: 2 per person daily and in possession north of Point Sur.
details: California halibut only; Pacific halibut has a different season and rules.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply. With rockfish or lingcod aboard, use one line and no more than two hooks; salmon aboard triggers salmon gear rules.
Fillets aboard: at least 16¾ in with all skin attached. Do not gaff an undersized fish.
Do not halve halibut fillets. A lengthwise midline split is allowed only if the pieces remain joined for at least two inches at one end; retain all skin and the minimum fillet length.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

salmon.name: Chinook salmon
salmon.season: Ocean salmon is closed in the Klamath Management Zone for the remainder of 2026.
salmon.bag: No retention while the Northern/Klamath recreational season is closed.
salmon.size: Not applicable during the 2026 closed season.
details: CDFW says the Klamath Management Zone remains closed for the rest of 2026; do not use a Central/Southern fall opener here.
Future seasons depend on federal and state action and require a new review.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

albacore.name: Albacore tuna
albacore.season: Year-round in reviewed 2026 state and federal rules, subject to current notices in U.S. waters north of Point Conception.
albacore.bag: 25 per person daily and in possession, in addition to the general 20-finfish limit.
albacore.size: No minimum size in these recreational rules.
details: The albacore limit drops to 10 south of Point Conception (34°27′ N). This card does not cover Mexico.
General ocean hook-and-line rules apply; fish already aboard can impose stricter rod and hook limits.
If processing tuna aboard south of Point Conception, follow the tuna-specific fillet, skin and bag-label requirements in §27.65. This card covers day trips; multi-day possession rules differ.
If any part of an albacore trip enters U.S. EEZ waters south of 34°27′ N, no more than 10 albacore per person may be onboard for that trip; the rule is not determined only by where a fish was caught.
Federal tuna limits apply per 24-hour period at sea and never authorize more than one daily bag per calendar day. Multi-day possession needs separate review.

South of Point Conception (34°27′ N), tuna processed aboard must use the six-piece arrangement required by §27.65, keep all skin attached, and be individually bagged with its species labeled. That specific six-piece rule does not apply to processing north of the line.

rod.note: This profile is for recreational rod-and-reel fishing from a boat. Read the species-specific hook, line, retention and on-board restrictions below.

dungeness.name: Dungeness crab
dungeness.season: Closed after Jul 31, 2026. Nov 7, 2026 is a scheduled reopening, subject to health and gear declarations.
dungeness.bag: When open: 10 per person daily; 10 in possession on a private boat.
dungeness.size: 5¾ in shell width, measured across the body just in front of the side spines, excluding those spines. Carry a crab gauge.
details: Season opening and trap permission are separate. Northern November trap clearance has not been confirmed; check CDFW whale-safe and health notices.
A crab-trap validation is required to use traps. Maximum 10 deployed traps per person; required escape rings, destruct device, GO ID and buoy markings apply.
Hoop nets and snares have separate gear rules. A trap restriction does not itself close those methods, but the season and health closures still apply.
Check the current 2026 hoop-net marking rules and all gear details in §29.80 before setting gear.
Crab traps may not be deployed during the seven days before the Dungeness season opens. Service deployed traps at intervals no greater than nine days, weather conditions permitting (§29.80(c)).
Crab loop traps or snares may have no more than six loops. Hoop nets must be raised and inspected at least every two hours (§29.80).

North of Point Arguello, each hoop net must have the required surface buoy marked with the operator’s GO ID; the main buoy may not exceed 6 in in diameter or 14 in in length. An optional orange marker marked H and its connecting line have additional marking specifications; check §29.80(b) before rigging.

trap.note: Trap permission is checked separately from the Dungeness season and health closures. Confirm the current recreational trap declaration, validation, marking and tending rules before setting.

hoop.note: A hoop net is a different gear category from a crab trap. Follow the current hoop-net construction, attendance and deployment rules; season and health closures still apply.

snare.note: Use the current snare definition and gear limits. A trap restriction does not by itself establish permission to take Dungeness; the season and health checks also apply.

pacific-halibut.name: Pacific halibut
pacific-halibut.season: Apr 1–Nov 15, 2026 north of Point Arena, or until the quota is reached earlier.
details: When angling, use no more than one line with two hooks attached.
Quota can close the season early; check the current CDFW halibut page and hotline before fishing.
Pacific halibut is distinct from California halibut; do not apply the two-fish California halibut limit.
Check the exact MPA, method and all other gear rules at the selected position and date.

rod.note: This profile covers recreational boat angling. One line with a maximum of two hooks; quota and geographic notices still apply.

area_notices.name: Northern California MPAs
area_notices.note: Pyramid Point, Point St. George Reef Offshore, Reading Rock and other MPAs have different take exceptions. Conservative app policy excludes them from fishing targets; exact coordinates and method-specific regulations still require review.

area_notices.name: Humboldt Bay and Cape Mendocino protected areas
area_notices.note: Samoa SMCA has narrow salmon, surf smelt and Dungeness take exceptions; South Humboldt Bay SMRMA and South Cape Mendocino SMR prohibit most take. Sugarloaf Island and Steamboat Rock have vessel-access restrictions. The app excludes mapped protected geometries from fishing targets; inspect exact CDFW boundaries and method/date exceptions.

limitations: Landing port is not a catch position; named grounds are broad reports, not GPS fixes.
Reports are a selected sample, with unknown effort and missing unsuccessful trips.
Satellite temperature and HF radar measure surface context, not bottom conditions.
Daily observations are not a seven-day bite forecast or live entrance clearance.
